title: Stochastic Perturbation Scorer and Robustness Prober for Quantized Profile Validation
creator: Aisha Martinez
description: Introduce a new evaluation component that injects controlled stochastic perturbations at multiple layers (tokenization, attention temperature, KV-cache warm/cold starts, and prompt paraphrase ensembles) to surface brittle failure modes introduced by FP8/INT8 quantization profiles. The prober will drive per-task scorers (perplexity, MMLU-style pass@k and accuracy suites, ROUGE/BLEU for generation, and domain-specific scorers for summarization/codegen) and emit robustness delta metrics and confidence intervals. The goal is to give calibration workflows a reproducible stress harness that augments existing deterministic evals and helps define gating thresholds for automated rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Stochastic prober integrated into the quantization calibration pipeline and runnable as a CI job (quant-calib-stress).
A2: Per-task scorer plugins implemented for perplexity, MMLU-style accuracy, ROUGE, BLEU, and a pluggable interface for custom scorers.

A3: Prober supports noise injection knobs: token-drop, token-replace-with-synonym, temperature jitter, KV cold-start probability, and prompt-paraphrase sampling. All knobs are configurable via YAML profile.
A4: Output includes 95% confidence intervals and a robustness delta compared to FP32 baseline for every metric; results stored to the eval metrics sink and visible on the quant-quality dashboard.
A5: A gating rule document that maps observed delta thresholds to rollout actions (approve/hold/rollback) is drafted and reviewed by Safety and Product.
A6: Unit and integration tests that simulate at least 3 stochastic settings and validate aggregator correctness are present and green.
A7: End-to-end latency and cost overhead documented; overhead under typical config must be <20% of deterministic eval job cost or justify trade-offs.
A8: Two sample runs demonstrating a representative FP8 profile and an INT8 profile with annotated findings are uploaded to the design doc.
tasks: T1: Design API for prober configuration and scorer plugin interface (YAML schema + Python SDK hooks).
T2: Implement tokenization-aware perturbation layer that operates before model input encoding (ensures deterministic seed control).
T3: Implement in-flight perturbation hooks for runtime-level effects (temperature jitter, KV cold-start).

T4: Develop scorer adapters: perplexity adapter, MMLU adapter (question/answer accuracy + pass@k), ROUGE and BLEU adapters with tokenization normalization, and custom summarization fidelity scorer (F1+coverage).
T5: Integrate outputs with existing eval metrics sink (ENG-31122 adapter bridge) and add schema fields for robustness_delta and ci_95.
T6: Build a small dashboard tile and Grafana panel for per-profile robustness deltas and CI bands (quant-quality dashboard).
T7: Create CI job config and resource sizing for running stochastic prober nightly on calibration branches.
T8: Write gating guidance and sample run notes for SRE/Product reviews.
notes: NOTE: We intentionally focus on additive stochastic probes rather than adversarial gradient-based attacks to keep compute requirements low and keep evaluations interpretable to PMs.
Trade-off: token-replacement with synonyms increases lexical variance but confounds BLEU; we normalize tokens beforehand and report both raw and normalized BLEU.
Decision: Use bootstrapped 95% CIs (B=1000 resamples) for robustness bands—agreed with Research to balance compute and statistical stability.
Follow-up: If a profile shows >2.5% MMLU drop with CI not overlapping baseline, trigger automatic hold in rollout pipeline (automation story tracked separately).
